Each jump turns at most 5 squares blue (the square it lands on plus up to 4 neighbors), so 3 jumps cover at most 15 < 16 squares. Thus at least 4 jumps are needed.

Four jumps suffice. Label squares (row, column) with rows and columns 1 to 4, and jump on (1,2), (2,4), (3,1), (4,3):
- (1,2) covers (1,1), (1,2), (1,3), (2,2)
- (2,4) covers (1,4), (2,4), (3,4), (2,3)
- (3,1) covers (2,1), (3,1), (4,1), (3,2)
- (4,3) covers (4,2), (4,3), (4,4), (3,3)

These 16 squares are all distinct, so the whole grid is covered.

ANSWER: 4
